drills.q: Given prerequisite pairs, determine whether all courses can be completed.
drills.a: Build a directed graph (prereq -> dependent), run Kahn's algorithm; if the processed count equals the total number of courses, yes; otherwise a cycle blocks some subset.

drills.q: Return a valid course completion order, or an empty list if impossible.
drills.a: Kahn's algorithm: queue all in-degree-0 nodes, pop and record each, decrement neighbor in-degrees, enqueue new zeros; return the recorded order if its length equals n, else empty.

drills.q: Implement topological sort using DFS, including cycle detection.
drills.a: Three-color DFS (white/gray/black); mark a node gray on entry, black on exit and push it onto a stack; a gray-to-gray edge is a cycle. Reverse the finished stack for the valid order.

drills.q: Given a sorted list of words in an unknown alien alphabet, reconstruct a valid character order.
drills.a: For each pair of adjacent words, find the first differing character and add a directed edge from the earlier character to the later one, then topologically sort the character graph; also detect the invalid case where a longer word's full prefix appears after it as a shorter word.

drills.q: Find the minimum number of semesters to complete all courses if any number of unblocked courses can be taken simultaneously.
drills.a: Run Kahn's algorithm processing one entire in-degree-zero frontier per round (layered BFS); the number of rounds until the queue empties is the answer; return -1 if a cycle prevents completion.

drills.q: Return the lexicographically smallest valid topological order of a DAG.
drills.a: Replace Kahn's plain queue with a min-heap keyed on node value, always popping the smallest currently-eligible (in-degree-0) node; runs in O((V+E) log V).
